talks.title: Elle Armageddon
talks.teaser: Examines elle Armageddon and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Overview: Elle Armageddon delivers the PancakesCon 3 keynote on workplace authenticity, challenging dress codes and appearance policies that discriminate against people of color and self-expression.

Key Topics: Director of security engineering leadership philosophy; mutual accountability and trusting team expertise; workplace policies policing appearance of people of color; visible tattoos and piercings acceptance; and building inclusive security teams.

Technical Details: Armageddon argues that professional appearance standards often police how people of color express cultural identity, punishing career advancement for authentic self-expression. She advocates retiring myths about visible tattoos and piercings.

Takeaways: Security industry culture must evolve beyond appearance-based gatekeeping. Leaders should foster environments where diverse team members can be authentic without career penalties.

talks.title: Andrew Lemon - Where the #$@! am I? Preparing to Take the Shot
talks.teaser: Outlines andrew Lemon - Where the #$@! am practitioners? Preparing to Take the Shot and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Red Team Scope and Mindset

Andrew Lemon of Alias Security walks through a full external red-team engagement to domain admin—aimed at newcomers who hear tool names but rarely see end-to-end tradecraft. Scope required initial compromise from outside, user and host access, privilege escalation, and an APT-style impact demonstration such as ransomware deployment while staying stealthy enough to give the SOC partial wins.

Reconnaissance and Initial Access

Lemon emphasizes scoping documents as the engagement lifeblood. He describes credential harvesting, VPN identification via DNS dumpster and Shodan, and testing both Windows and Linux VPN clients to establish internal network presence without triggering unnecessary alerts.

Internal Mapping

Once inside, he locates domain controllers using patient DNS techniques—adding customer resolvers, guessing predictable hostnames like dc01.domain.com, and leveraging nltest and WS-Management from non-domain-joined systems via RunAs token creation with compromised credentials.

Escalation Path

The narrative progresses to SharpHound collection for BloodHound analysis, acknowledging some steps are intentionally loud. Lemon's core message: real engagements chain mundane recon, credential reuse, and Active Directory mapping—not only exotic exploits.

talks.title: John Strand
talks.teaser: Presents john Strand and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Why deception belongs early

John Strand argues cyber deception is essential now, not something to defer until perfect defenses exist. Homogeneous endpoint and firewall stacks make attacker bypass predictable; deception adds randomness and risk for adversaries.

Easy starting points

He highlights Thinkst Canary Tokens for simple callback artifacts (documents, PDFs, S3 buckets) and the DARPA-funded ADHD VM bundling deception tools from Black Hills Information Security and Secure Ideas.

Catching cloned login pages

Embedded JavaScript on authentication pages detects when a cloned site loads outside the real domain and phones home, exposing attacker IPs before phishing emails send. Black Hills uses a private Canary server and has caught active clone attempts.

Beyond login traps

Strand contrasts stale IOC feeds with real-time, organization-specific intelligence from deception, and describes bait documents on shares with keywords like passwords or SCADA to trap post-exploitation search tools.

talks.title: Dave Weinstein - What to look for in a manager, and pottery!
talks.teaser: Presents dave Weinstein - What to look for in a manager, and pottery and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Choosing a manager

Dave Weinstein, with nearly 34 years in tech, pairs career advice with pottery—acknowledging deep expertise in ceramics but only solid knowledge of management. He frames manager selection as a high-stakes decision made with interview-level information asymmetry.

Due diligence like hiring

Candidates should scrutinize managers the way companies scrutinize them: check social media, seek references, and prefer leaders they or trusted colleagues have worked with before. Hiring managers conduct far more interviews than candidates, so preparation matters.

Feedback and advocacy

Good managers trumpet your successes publicly while coaching weaknesses privately—"constructive feedback" should not mean praise is worthless. Some behaviors require immediate public response and HR reporting, but routine improvement belongs in private mentorship. It is healthy if managers aspire to return to individual contributor roles someday.
